newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine inflation seen steady to year-end.
newsitem.headline: Philippine inflation seen steady to year-end.

text.p: The Philippine inflation rate is likely to remain steady until the end of the year provided the government remains resistant to pressures for a wage hike, analysts said.
The analysts' forecasts followed the government's announcement on Tuesday that October inflation was lower than expected at 4.7 percent year-on-year, against 4.4 percent the previous month.
A Reuter consensus survey of six stock brokers last week had shown October inflation was expected to be at 5.28 percent.
"The numbers are very positive. We are beginning to see the results of sound fiscal and monetary policies, and some good luck," Manuel Goseco, economist at Dharmala Securities said.

The Philippines has, in the past few years, been hit by typhoons and floods in the later part of each year and a severe bout of bad weather last November had boosted inflation to double-digit levels. But the country has been spared from such natural disasters this year.
Inflation tapered down to a single-digit level in June.

Analysts said their expectations for higher October inflation was based on fears of typhoons as well as the effect of recent local oil price hikes. But the figures for October had renewed hopes the government's target of average inflation of 8.7 percent for the year would be met, they said.

"We expect some slowdown (in inflation) for the rest of the year, and maybe up to early next year," Joy Quintos, research head of the Philippine representative office of Prime East Securities Hong Kong Ltd said.
